ShortDescription.Value: One bar showing the state of your city, where every reading opens what it is about.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Seety
Maybe the real city was the stats we saw along the way.
## Setup
1. Enable the mod. 2. Click the **gear** at the end of the bar. 3. Click the readings you want to keep. Click the gear again.
That is the whole configuration. You pick by clicking the thing itself, not by hunting a name in a list of checkboxes.
Drag the bar anywhere. It stays where you put it.
## The bar
**Twenty-six readings**, all off or on as you like: happiness, health, unemployment, homelessness, workers, tourists, active problems, electricity, water delivered, sewage taken away, crematorium coverage, cemetery space, four school levels, parking, garbage processing, safety, fire safety, environment quality, post, traffic flow, land value, zone demand and public transport.
Three of those carry a second figure rather than a square of their own, because they are one question asked twice: health also holds hospital coverage, garbage also holds landfill space, and safety also holds free jail and prison cells. Open the reading and both are there, each still opening its own info view.
Two rules decide what is on that list:
- **It is not already on the vanilla HUD.** Population, money and income are on screen permanently, so repeating them buys you nothing and costs width. - **It mirrors the exact source the game uses for the same figure.** A number that disagrees with the game's own panels is worse than no number at all.
**More is always better.** Half of what a city reports is naturally negative - pollution, crime, cells occupied, schools filling up. Those are turned around and renamed, so a fuller, greener bar always means better. There is no direction to remember per icon.
Cross a sensible limit and a reading turns amber, then red. Thresholds stay quiet in an empty city, because nobody living there yet is not a crisis.
## Everything opens something
This is the part that matters. **Click a reading and it takes you to what it is about.**
Most open the matching in-game info view. The rest open a window - draggable, closeable, with its own place on screen:
> **Active problems** - every notification grouped by type and counted, worst first. Click a type and the camera goes to one of them; click again and it goes to the next, so you can work through them instead of hunting. A switch in the title bar hides the notification icons floating over the city.
> **Workers** - your workforce and the jobs that exist, on the same rows. Twelve columns: people by education, who is a child, a student, retired or of working age; who is employed, idle, working below their qualification, working outside the city or commuting in; and beside them the jobs at each level and how many nobody is doing. Every citizen counted one by one.
> **Happiness and demographics** - who actually lives here, age against education, with each band's share of the population drawn under it. A wide band of seniors is a wave of retirements coming; a wide band of teenagers is a school problem arriving in a few years.
> **Zone demand** - all six demands, and behind each one the five biggest reasons it sits where it does. Open the commercial, industrial or office one and the bar comes apart per resource: what the city actually wants, how many businesses trade in it, how stocked their shelves are and how staffed they are. The game tracks all of it and never draws it, so a flat commercial bar stops being a mystery. Where a resource has a company behind it, the row is clickable - it names the one losing the most ground and flies you to it.
> **Schools**, **transport**, **traffic**, **parking** and **environment** each open a list of their own: the fullest schools first, passengers and freight by mode, the worst jams by vehicle kind - click one to fly there - and the parts behind the combined readings. Where the game has its own panel for one of them, clicking goes there.
Some readings also carry a chart of how they got here.
## What it never does
Seety reads. It does not govern.
The bar itself writes nothing: the only things clicking a reading changes are which info view is showing and where the camera is pointing.
There is exactly one exception, and it is nowhere near the bar. The options page has a field to add (or remove) money from your treasury, City Watchdog style - off to the side, typed in on purpose. Everything described above this line still reads and only reads; this is the one deliberate control that does not, and it never fires on its own.
## Before you install
English only for now. Free and open source under the MIT licence: [source on GitHub](https://github.com/merrinaf-tech/Seety).
If it saves you a few trips through the menus, you can [buy me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/fabiozsche). Entirely optional - the mod is the same either way.
Publish.ChangeLog:
The bar no longer comes back after being switched off in the options.
Dragging follows the pointer on every screen. Above 1080p the bar moved further than the cursor - twice as far at 4K - and could be dragged off the edge and left there. Windows too.
The bar is shorter, and sits level with the buttons along the top of the HUD.
Empty lists are drawn inside their window instead of below it, and the traffic window no longer opens blank in a city with no jams.
In Workers, the Kids column no longer reads zero at the education levels where adults are studying.
The problem list is rebuilt only while its window is open, instead of twice a second for the whole game.
